newsitem.title: UK: BA says cargo load factor holding up.
newsitem.headline: BA says cargo load factor holding up.

text.p: British Airways Plc cargo load factor is "holding up very well" on its passenger flights operating out of London's Heathrow and Gatwick airports, a BA World Cargo spokesman said.

Flights have been hit by a 72-hour strike of BA cabin crew which started earlier on Wednesday, but "we have 31 percent of flights operating from Heathrow and 84 percent from Gatwick," the spokesman added.
"Flights to the Far East are virtually full and the overall cargo load factor on long-haul flights is over 70 percent," the spokesman said.
BA Cargo handles a weekly average of 9,000 tonnes of air freight at Heathrow and 4,000 tonnes at Gatwick, he added.
On July 7, BA said its scheduled freighter flights will operate normally during the strike and that they would not seek to obtain extra cargo space from other airlines.

BA's cargo schedule comprises weekly Nairobi-London Stansted and Stansted-Johannesburg flights with a DC-8 freighter leased from African International Airways and three-times weekly Stansted-Hong Kong return flights, operated with a 747F wet-leased from U.S. carrier Atlas Air.
Wet-leasing covers the hire of aircraft and crew and usually also includes insurance and maintenance.
It also operates three-times weekly London Heathrow-Tokyo flights jointly with Japan Airlines, using its 747 freighter aircraft.

Other cargo services are twice-weekly London-Singapore and London-Seoul 747 freighter services operated in conjunction with Singapore Airlines and Korean Air and using the other carrier's aircraft. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
